what_happened: The ego ended up about 5 m left of the recorded path, even though the command was RIGHT, and kept driving in that lane behind the slower vehicle 87. It only eased from 5.6 to 3.8 m/s while the gap shrank from 11.4 m to 4.6 m, and its front hit 87. The lead car looked smeared in the camera because the ego was far from where the real car drove, but it was still visible and clearly ahead in the lane.

After handoff, the ego drifted about 4.6 m left of its recorded path, which went right (command RIGHT), and ended up in the lane behind slow actor 87. It eased off only from 5.6 to 4.2 m/s while the gap shrank from 11.9 to 4.7 m, and its front hit 87's rear. The lead car was smeared in the camera view but still clearly visible.

The route command was RIGHT and the recorded path went into the right-hand lanes, but after handoff the ego stayed about 7–8 m left of it in a left lane. Its plan kept drifting further left, and at 10.6 s it ran onto the edge of the median island at about 5.8 m/s. No actor was hit; the nearest car ahead was still 27 m away. The left side of the camera view smears because the ego is so far from where the real car drove.

After the policy took over at 4.6 s, the ego braked hard on a clear highway (16.8 to 8.1 m/s) while the gap to the lead car (18) was growing, and its planned path veered left toward the adjacent lane. Because it slowed down, the ego fell back alongside actor 1 in the left lane, and its leftward drift caused a side collision with that car at 6.5 s; the ego was also rear-ended because of the sudden braking.

After handoff the ego braked hard for no clear reason (17→8 m/s with the lead pulling away), falling about 10 m behind the recorded position. At the same time its plan drifted left, and it sideswiped actor 1, which was driving in the left lane and had come alongside because the ego slowed.

The ego drifted about 5 m left of the recorded path (a RIGHT command, while the logged car was one lane to the right) and stayed in that lane behind slower actor 87. The gap to 87 shrank from 11.5 m to 4.4 m while the ego only slowed from 5.5 to 4.0 m/s, and its front hit 87. Actor 87 was smeared in the camera view but still clearly visible, so the policy should have braked.

Approaching a signalized intersection with a RIGHT command, the ego stayed in the leftmost lane next to the raised median, about 7–8 m left of where the human drove (several lanes to the right). Its planned path then bent further left, and at 10.0 s it clipped the nose of the median island at about 6 m/s while slowing.

The ego drove about 5 m to the left of the recorded path, in the lane of slower vehicle 87, and closed on it from 8.8 m to 4.4 m. It only slowed gently (5.0 to 3.8 m/s), its planned path ran straight into 87, and it hit 87's rear with its front at 11.0 s.

Driving straight in its lane, the ego held about 4.2 m/s while the lead vehicle (actor 66) slowed to near a stop, and the gap closed from about 10.7 m to contact. After the policy took over at 4.7 s with about 8.6 m of gap, it barely slowed (4.2 to 4.1 m/s) and hit actor 66's rear with its front.

The ego was going straight on a multi-lane arterial at about 4.2 m/s. The lead car in its lane (actor 66) slowed to nearly a stop, and the gap fell from 10.7 m to 4.3 m over about 1.5 s. After taking over at 4.7 s, the policy kept the same speed and planned a move into the left lane instead of braking, and its front ran into actor 66 at 5.6 s.

After handoff on the highway, the ego braked hard for no clear reason, from 16.8 to 8.1 m/s, even though the gap to lead vehicle 18 was growing. At the same time it drifted left off the recorded path, which went slightly right, and sideswiped vehicle 1 as that car came alongside in the left lane. The hard braking also likely caused the separate rear contact.

With a RIGHT command, the ego stayed in a left through lane about 4–8 m left of the recorded path, which went toward the right-side lanes. Its plan then bent further left, and while slowing (8→6 m/s) it ran onto the nose of the median island before the intersection at 10.0 s. The camera view was clean, and lead car 9 was 34 m or more ahead, so nothing outside the policy forced this.

In slow freeway traffic (about 1–2 m/s), the ego's planned path (orange) swung left toward the adjacent left lane, even though the route command was RIGHT. The ego edged left and its front-left corner clipped actor 23, which was travelling alongside in that lane, at 9.6 s. The nearest car ahead in the ego's lane was about 21 m away, so this was not a rear-end of a lead vehicle.

Driving straight at about 4.2 m/s, the ego closed on actor 66, which had stopped in its lane: the gap fell from 10.7 m to 4.3 m between 4.1 s and 5.6 s. The policy took over at 4.7 s, kept its speed without braking (its plan swerved left toward actor 61 instead) and hit 66 with its front 0.9 s later. The ego was only 0.2 m off the recorded human path, so the replayed actor 66 probably didn't move as it did in the real drive, and the ego was also rear-ended at some point.

The ego was slowing in slow highway traffic (3.4 to 1.1 m/s) and its planned path kept wobbling to the left. It edged over the left lane line, about 1.4 m off the recorded path, and its front-left corner hit vehicle 23, which was alongside in the adjacent left lane. The lead car was still about 20 m ahead, so this was not a following-distance collision.

The ego was replaying the logged trajectory at about 8 m/s and closing on lead vehicle 1 in the same lane, which was slower. The policy took over at 4.6 s, when the boxes were nearly touching, and the front collision was logged 0.2 s later even though the ego had started braking (7.9 to 7.4 m/s). The collision was already unavoidable at handoff, and the lead actor in the sim had probably drifted from where it was in the recorded drive.

The ego was slowing in heavy freeway traffic (4.1 to 1.5 m/s) when its planned path wiggled left, toward actor 23 in the next lane to the left. By 9.4 s the ego had drifted about 1.4 m off the recorded human path and its front-left corner hit that car while the lane ahead was clear (lead vehicle 10 was about 21 m away). The left-side camera view of 23 was smeared but still readable as a car, and the rear-end contact came later.
